summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a complex medical history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic G-tube and TPN dependence, and a history of upper extremity DVTs was admitted for dark-brown G-tube output concerning for gastrointestinal bleeding. She had been on Lovenox for anticoagulation and had a history of prior GI bleeds. Initial evaluation showed guaiac-positive drainage and stable hemoglobin. An endoscopy revealed mild G-tube-related gastritis with no active bleeding, and a small bowel endoscopy was unremarkable. Blood cultures showed no growth, and a urine culture grew Streptococcus anginosus, which was not treated due to lack of symptoms. She was not on IV antibiotics as her recent Enterococcus avium line infection had been completed. Suicidal ideation expressed in the ED was evaluated and cleared by psychiatry. She remained on home medications including ranitidine, anticoagulation, and pain management with gabapentin and amitriptyline. TPN was held during admission and planned for restart at home. She was discharged home with services, stable and with no active bleeding.
